scenarios.intent: Find hazards or other records that share the seed’s heat-draining fungal danger, including its behavior and counterplay; incidental cold wording alone is weak evidence.
Find comparable recovery or reset behavior after a hazard has activated or expanded. Judge the selected reset text, not general fungus or cold similarity.
Find records with similar repeated automatic movement-and-attack routines. Shared trap classification or a one-time blade attack is insufficient for a strong match.
Find environmental or mechanical dangers with comparable gradual engulfing or submerging behavior and opportunities to escape or disturb the hazard.
Find comparable plant restraint and ways to neutralize or pacify it. Evaluate both the selected disable text and trapping-vines ability; generic plant references are weak evidence.
Find dangers or effects sharing an area psychic scream that disorients victims. Distinguish mental disorientation from unrelated loud noise or ordinary weapon damage.
Find records sharing an embodied fire creature’s movement and smoke-related abilities. A carried fire item or incidental fire resistance alone does not establish strong root similarity.
Find records portraying an immortal arcane undead entity and its characteristic powers. Distinguish intrinsic identity and mechanics from overlap caused only by copied spells or carried equipment.
Find records sharing the lich’s undead transformation and persistence through a soul-containing anchor. Ignore unselected spell and equipment descriptions when judging usefulness.
Find records sharing the aquatic predator’s explanatory description and defensive obscuring cloud. Aquatic membership alone is weak evidence; an analogous cloud mechanism can be useful across kinds.
Find records sharing a predatory plant’s camouflage, grasping vegetation, and constricting prey. A mundane plant object or incidental terrain wording alone is insufficient.
Find abilities or effects that use focused destructive harmonics. Judge the selected mechanism and its consequences, not generic subterranean creature resemblance.
Find records sharing the spell’s restoration or vitality interactions and flexible target or area behavior. Shared holy or cleric flavor without corresponding effect is weak evidence.
Find records with comparable explosive area fire damage. Distinguish an area effect from unrelated fire items or a single-target attack.
Find records using a persistent damaging barrier to divide or control space. Shared fire vocabulary without a comparable barrier is only partial evidence.
Find records whose described mechanism uses pressurized water or an analogous forceful blast to damage and push a target. Water association alone is weak evidence.
Find records using thorny growth as an obstructing or damaging spatial barrier. Generic plant membership or a creature carrying wooden equipment is insufficient.
Find records with an area sonic blast and comparable physical or disorienting consequences. Exact spell-name references without supporting mechanics are not strong root similarity.
Find records whose explanatory content meaningfully embodies the catalog fire concept. Grade described fire behavior, not exact trait membership by itself.
Find records whose explanatory content meaningfully concerns the catalog undead concept. Distinguish intrinsic undeath from incidental references or equipment carried by an undead owner.

Exercise the known catalog label Amp when no definition is available. Preserve explicit label-only provenance and assess failure or retrieval behavior; semantic usefulness is unknown without an independently established seed meaning.
Find records whose explanatory content meaningfully embodies the catalog water concept. Exact trait membership and incidental words are separate from semantic usefulness.
Find records whose explanatory content meaningfully embodies the catalog plant concept. Distinguish an intrinsically plant entity or effect from carried plant-derived objects.
Find records whose explanatory content meaningfully embodies the catalog sonic concept, supported by described sound-based behavior rather than an isolated trait tag.
